title: A Gravity for the Terminal
premise: When gravity fails for nine seconds across the Meridian system, cargo hauler Cyrus Almeida's ship is thrown into a debris field that shouldn't exist — the wreckage of the colony ship Halcyon, officially lost with all hands twelve years ago. Among the dead he finds a survivor in cryo, Dr. Ilsa Voss, who carries proof that the terraforming consortium murdered four thousand colonists to cover a failed atmospheric experiment. As Cyrus and Ilsa race to broadcast the truth, they discover the nine-second gravity flicker was no accident but a weapon test, and the consortium will erase an entire moon — and everyone on it — to keep the secret. Cyrus must choose between delivering Ilsa to safety and staying to hold the evidence beacon long enough for the truth to escape; he stays, and dies transmitting, while Ilsa carries his memory logs and the massacre's record to a system finally forced to listen.
about_author: Sebastian Crane is the pen name of a former maritime logistics analyst who spent a decade writing technical manuals before turning to fiction about people who move things through dangerous places. They live near a working port and write at night, when the cranes stop moving.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds of Falling
chapters.summary: Cyrus Almeida, hauling seed stock to the terraforming station Verdance, experiences total gravitational failure for exactly nine seconds. His ship drifts off-course into uncharted space. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: quiet dread beneath routine — a man who has survived twenty years by trusting schedules.

chapters.title: The Garden for No One
chapters.summary: Flashback woven into present: Cyrus tends Verdance's orbital greenhouse, built for colonists who never arrived after the Halcyon disaster. He talks to plants because there's no one else. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as devotion.

chapters.title: Debris Where Nothing Should Be
chapters.summary: Recovering from the drift, Cyrus detects a dense debris field absent from every chart — hull plating bearing Halcyon registry marks. His proximity alarm screams as wreckage tumbles past. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: disbelief curdling into fear.

chapters.title: What the Records Say
chapters.summary: Cyrus cross-references port databases: the Halcyon was declared lost to reactor failure twelve years ago, all 4,000 aboard confirmed dead, site sealed. Yet this field shows weapons scarring. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: the first crack in his trust in authority.

chapters.title: A Heartbeat in the Cold
chapters.summary: Following a faint distress transponder, Cyrus finds an intact cryo pod wedged in wreckage: Dr. Ilsa Voss, Halcyon's atmospheric scientist, alive. Reviving her risks both their lives. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: compassion overriding self-preservation.

chapters.title: Ilsa Wakes
chapters.summary: Ilsa surfaces from cryo disoriented, grieving, furious — she remembers the attack. She tells Cyrus the reactor story is a lie and that she hid data proving it inside the pod itself. POV: Ilsa. Emotional beat: rage sharpened by twelve years of frozen helplessness.

chapters.title: The Consortium's Smile
chapters.summary: At Verdance, station administrator Ondine Marsh welcomes Cyrus warmly — too warmly — asking precise questions about his drift trajectory. Cyrus lies for the first time in his career. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: guilt and adrenaline of deception.

chapters.title: Data in the Dark
chapters.summary: Hidden in his cargo bay, Ilsa decrypts her pod's archive: sensor logs, internal comms, orders signed by consortium director Aurel Kestrel authorizing 'asset denial' on the Halcyon. POV: Ilsa. Emotional beat: vindication shadowed by horror at what she's re-reading.

chapters.title: Cargo Manifest Lies
chapters.summary: Cyrus uses his hauler credentials to move Ilsa between stations hidden in legitimate freight. We see the machinery of contested orbits — checkpoints, bribes, silent complicity. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: a decent man learning how much rot his competence has been serving.

chapters.title: The Man Who Checks
chapters.summary: Consortium investigator Dario Fen tracks the anomaly of Cyrus's drift. Cold, methodical, genuinely believing order requires the Halcyon stay buried. POV: Dario. Emotional beat: antagonist established as conviction, not cartoonish evil.

chapters.title: Verdance Under Watch
chapters.summary: Marsh searches Cyrus's quarters and finds nothing — but plants a tracker anyway. Cyrus notices the greenhouse humidity logs have been altered, someone covering traces of his absence. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: paranoia taking root in a place that was sanctuary.

chapters.title: Four Thousand Names
chapters.summary: Ilsa reads aloud the passenger manifest she memorized before boarding the pod — names, faces, the children in hydroponics class she taught. Cyrus listens all night. POV: Ilsa. Emotional beat: grief transformed into testimony; the two grow close.

chapters.title: The Beacon Problem
chapters.summary: Broadcasting the evidence requires the old relay array at Bastion Rock, decommissioned and monitored. Any transmission longer than minutes will be traced. They plan anyway. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: hope as a calculated risk.

chapters.title: Gravity Flickers Again
chapters.summary: A second, localized gravity failure hits a mining platform, killing forty-seven. Official cause: equipment fault. Ilsa recognizes the signature — the same waveform as the nine-second event. It's a weapon being calibrated. POV: Ilsa. Emotional beat: realization that more massacres are scheduled.

chapters.title: Fen Closes In
chapters.summary: Dario Fen links Cyrus's drift to the debris field and requests authority to detain him. Kestrel approves, ordering the hauler's next route pre-loaded with a trap. POV: Dario. Emotional beat: the net tightening with bureaucratic calm.

chapters.title: The Trap at Thessaly Gate
chapters.summary: Cyrus walks into the checkpoint ambush but his twenty years of cargo cunning save him — he swaps manifests, dumps decoy mass, threads a customs gap. Ilsa nearly dies shielding the data core. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: terror and exhilaration; they're fugitives now, fully.

chapters.title: What Survival Costs
chapters.summary: Hiding in a derelict fuel depot, Ilsa confronts Cyrus: he abandoned his contract, his garden, his clean record. He admits he doesn't know who he is without the work. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: love beginning, priced in everything each has lost.

chapters.title: Kestrel's Version
chapters.summary: Director Aurel Kestrel argues to her board that the Halcyon experiment's failure would have collapsed colonization funding for a generation; the deaths were tragic arithmetic. She orders Bastion Rock sterilized. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: chillingly reasonable villainy.

chapters.title: Allies in the Underside
chapters.summary: Cyrus reaches old smuggling contacts — dockworker Rhea Okonkwo and her independent hauler cell — who agree to shield them, at growing personal risk. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: solidarity among the people the system moves but never sees.

chapters.title: The Archive Within the Garden
chapters.summary: Twist: Ilsa discovers a second copy of her data was seeded into Verdance's agricultural AI years ago — the garden Cyrus tended holds the massacre's memory. The place he mourned becomes the weapon. POV: Ilsa. Emotional beat: awe; the theme made literal.

chapters.title: Marsh's Choice
chapters.summary: Administrator Marsh finds the planted tracker pinging from the derelict and realizes the consortium intends to erase Verdance too — with her on it. She hesitates between loyalty and survival. POV: Marsh. Emotional beat: complicity cracking.

chapters.title: Bastion Rock Approach
chapters.summary: The run to the relay array through patrol corridors, using a funeral barge as cover. Tense silence, near-detection, Rhea's crew holding steady. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: dread braided with resolve.

chapters.title: First Transmission
chapters.summary: They begin broadcasting the evidence in fragments. Ninety seconds in, Fen's strike team arrives early — Kestrel moved up the timeline. They transmit only a third before fleeing. POV: Ilsa. Emotional beat: triumph curdling into catastrophe.

chapters.title: The Story That Didn't Take
chapters.summary: The partial broadcast is dismissed as pirate hoax; consortium counter-narrative floods the nets within hours. Allies waver. One hauler cell defects. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: despair — truth alone isn't enough.

chapters.title: Fen Interrogates Rhea
chapters.summary: Rhea is captured and questioned by Fen, who offers her crew amnesty for Cyrus's location. She gives him nothing but a lesson in dockworker stubbornness. POV: Rhea. Emotional beat: defiance as dignity.

chapters.title: The Nine-Second Signature
chapters.summary: Ilsa completes her analysis: the gravity weapon's next full-system test is scheduled in six days — and its calibration target is Verdance orbit. The garden, the greenhouse, everyone. POV: Ilsa. Emotional beat: the clock starts; stakes become existential.

chapters.title: Kestrel and Fen
chapters.summary: Kestrel pressures Fen to stop thinking like an investigator and start acting like a soldier. Fen's faith in ordered sacrifice begins to fray when he sees the Verdance casualty projections. POV: Dario. Emotional beat: the antagonist's first doubt.

chapters.title: Everything We Carried
chapters.summary: Quiet chapter before the endgame: Cyrus and Ilsa inventory what remains — the data core, the manifest names, each other. They admit love plainly, without promise of tomorrow. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: tenderness under sentence of death.

chapters.title: The Plan That Requires Staying
chapters.summary: Full broadcast needs sustained uplink from Bastion Rock — hours, not minutes — meaning someone must hold the array manually against incoming assault. Everyone knows who will volunteer. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: sacrifice taking shape as a decision already half-made.

chapters.title: Marsh Defects
chapters.summary: Marsh delivers Verdance's internal security codes to Cyrus and warns of the weapon test, choosing the colonists over her career. Her defection gives them the timing window they need. POV: Marsh. Emotional beat: redemption purchased at the price of everything she was.

chapters.title: Storming the Silence
chapters.summary: Rhea's remaining cell runs interference across three checkpoints to draw Fen's fleet wide, buying the approach window. Costly, chaotic, heroic. POV: Rhea. Emotional beat: ordinary people spending themselves for a stranger's truth.

chapters.title: Bastion Rock, Second Attempt
chapters.summary: Cyrus and Ilsa reach the array under fire. Uplink established. The assault force is ninety seconds out. Ilsa begins the full transmission; Cyrus takes the manual stabilizer position. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: calm at the edge of annihilation.

chapters.title: Hold the Line
chapters.summary: The battle for the array. Cyrus keeps the dish aligned through direct hits, narrating the manifest names into the open channel as armor plates burn away around him. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: transcendence — the gardener planting one last crop.

chapters.title: The Truth Gets Out
chapters.summary: Transmission completes: logs, orders, names, the weapon's schedule, broadcast to every receiver in the system. Public channels ignite. Fen receives the order to fire on the array anyway. POV: Ilsa. Emotional beat: victory and horror arriving simultaneously.

chapters.title: Fen Breaks
chapters.summary: Fen refuses the fire order, arrests his own strike commander, and broadcasts his authentication codes to verify the evidence — the investigator becoming witness. POV: Dario. Emotional beat: conscience outlasting loyalty.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds Forever
chapters.summary: Kestrel triggers the weapon early rather than lose control. Gravity fails across Verdance orbit — but Marsh's codes let the station brace, and the test's failure is witnessed by millions instead of covered up. Cyrus does not survive the array's destruction. POV: Ilsa. Emotional beat: grief and vindication fused.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Light
chapters.summary: Kestrel arrested by her own security council; hearings begin. Ilsa, hollowed out, drifts through the victory she bought with Cyrus's life. The system knows the Halcyon's four thousand names now. POV: Ilsa. Emotional beat: survivor's weight.

chapters.title: The Garden, Replanted
chapters.summary: Months later, Verdance's greenhouse reopens — this time for living colonists. Ilsa takes over tending it, reading Cyrus's plant logs, finding his handwriting in the margins. POV: Ilsa. Emotional beat: mourning becoming cultivation.

chapters.title: A Gravity for the Terminal
chapters.summary: Ilsa broadcasts a memorial each year on the anniversary of the nine seconds, ending with Cyrus's final transmitted words. The system pauses — all traffic, all orbits — for nine seconds of silence. POV: Ilsa. Emotional beat: love outlasting duty; memory as gravity.

chapters.title: Epilogue: What Survives
chapters.summary: Years on, a child born on Verdance asks Ilsa who Cyrus Almeida was. She answers with the manifest, the garden, and the story. Somewhere in the archives, his voice still reads names into the dark. POV: Ilsa. Emotional beat: quiet, earned hope — the price paid forward.
